_comment: Ablation config for NeRF-DS (WITH mask, ignore_mask=false), parameter under test = sparse_anchor.anchor_stride (see the 'ablation' section below). Based on configs_nerf_ds_with_mask.json. iterations=20000 (half the 40000-iter with-mask baseline, matching the user's wish for a more representative budget than a short proxy run) pushes total sweep time to ~55-60h on a 20GB H100 (7 scenes x 4 stride values) -- explicitly accepted by the user over shrinking scope, see full_ablation.py's docstring for the full time-budget derivation. anchor_stride itself is NOT read from this file's sparse_anchor.anchor_stride at run time: full_ablation.py overrides it per run via train.py's --anchor_stride CLI flag (CLI always wins over configs.json, see arguments/__init__.py's ParamGroup), the value here is only the fallback default if the script is ever invoked oddly. densify_grad_threshold/densify_until_iter/knn_k/coarse_levels are DELIBERATELY left at their memory-safe values (not scaled up with iterations): peak VRAM is set by max(N)*max(M) reached DURING densification/anchor-refinement, not by how many extra steady-state iterations follow it, so keeping densify_until_iter=6000 (well before iterations=20000) preserves the same OOM safety margin validated for anchor_stride=4 (the most memory-hungry sweep value) while letting optimization run longer at the final N/M.

ablation._comment: 4 values x 7 nerf_ds scenes = 28 runs. Smaller stride = more anchors = slower/heavier; larger stride = fewer anchors = faster/lighter -- the sweep deliberately spans both sides of the with-mask baseline default (8).
